The stand

Worth pulling off the highway

One little grey building with a red OPEN light, string bulbs on the eave and a lot with actual room in it.

  • The stand sits in the Eagles lot — a full parking lot, not a curb cut.
  • Drivers pull in, get through the window and roll back out to 410 without unhooking anything.
  • Regulars in trucks and work rigs are most of the 4 a.m. line.
  • Dillanos Coffee Roasters — the Roast Magazine Roaster of the Year placard hangs right in the window.
  • Roasted down the valley in Sumner, so it doesn't cross the country to get here.
  • Same beans they pull at the window are bagged for taking home.
  • Two hands in a small window and no lobby to manage.
  • Reviewers keep saying the same thing — the line looks long, then it isn't.
  • Order at the glass, pay at the glass, gone.

The window

They know the order before you say it

The coffee is the reason people stop the first time. The women in the window are the reason they keep stopping.

Customers write about the same faces year after year — one reviewer counted eight years and three baristas who still remember exactly how she takes it. Another says her mom has been through this window every single day for years, and got the whole family hooked.

It's a fifty-square-foot building on a state highway, and somehow it's the friendliest counter in Buckley.

Getting one

Three steps, no app

  1. Turn into the Eagles lot

    Off Highway 410 at the Hinkleman Extension end of town — the reader board is the landmark.

  2. Pull up to the window

    Order at the glass. Big drinks, small window, quick line.

  3. Back out on the highway

    Two minutes and you're pointed east again.
